name: Otto I crowned Holy Roman Emperor
summary: Pope John XII crowns Otto I in St Peter's, reviving the Western imperial title that had lapsed after the deposition of Berengar of Friuli in 924. The Privilegium Ottonianum re-defines the emperor's role as protector of the papacy and confirms imperial authority over papal elections.

_quarry.structural_significance: Founding moment of the Holy Roman Empire as a continuous institution. Otto's combination of German kingship + Italian kingdom + imperial dignity becomes the standard 'three crowns' of every German emperor for 600 years.
